There are always different takes on money. My dad was a financial advisor and always told me that a home loan was the cheapest loan you could get, with investment returns easily surpassing the interest rate. But that requires you to be into the long term investing game (or pay someone to get you there). And others take a lot of personal comfort from having a home "paid off". So, what kind of person are you?

Wait, first, do you have the Basic emergency savings? Forever ago it was 3 months living, these days I cringe anytime we have less than a year. Other loans with higher interest? Deferred maintenance on anything (old cars, house)?

If those are covered, then it's a personal call. Investments (done right they should return 10%, get lucky and you'll be above that) are the logical call, but the mortgage is easy and has a different kind of "feel good". What would I do? probably the mortgage even though I know it's not making the best use of the money.

Low seven figures in savings between the wife and I. We're quite blessed, but that's money we don't plan on touching for another 20 years or so.

Guess I'll just dump it into the Schwab Intelligent Portolios I'm screwing around with lately instead of the mortgage.

Thanks for your perspective.

Damn, good for you. Yeah, in that situation I would absolutely put it into investments.

I'm on the other end of the scale, my house only cost $65k... :) But I also don't work and my wife only works 3 days a week so we get a lot of time to Travel. $10k is 5 months of living without skimping. Heck, if I had a spare $10k, I'd be sorely tempted to take 2~3 months off to live in another country. We did a 3-month ski vacation a couple years back and it was Amazing having the vast expanse of time.

We plan on staying in this house for the foreseeable future. About $200k left on a 15y mortgage @ ~4%-ish.

Is it more prudent to pay off a mortgage sooner, or but towards investments ?

We already made an additional $10k principle payment towards the mortgage earlier this year, and I was thinking of making another one.

No outstanding debts save for the mortgage.
